steps.prompt: A newspaper says "about $500$ people came" when $487$ came. Why do people round numbers?

cards.title: Nearest ten, nearest hundred
cards.body: To round to the nearest ten, look at the ones digit: $0$ to $4$ rounds down, $5$ to $9$ rounds up. $47$ is nearer $50$ than $40$. For the nearest hundred, look at the tens digit: $487 \to 500$.

cards.title: Worked example: round 364
cards.problem: Round $364$ to the nearest ten and to the nearest hundred.

steps.text: Nearest ten: the ones digit is $4$, so round down.

try.prompt: What is $364$ to the nearest ten?

steps.text: Nearest hundred: the tens digit is $6$, so round up.

try.prompt: What is $364$ to the nearest hundred?

steps.text: Picture a number line from $300$ to $400$: $364$ is past the middle, $350$.

cards.title: Worked example: step to the next ten
cards.problem: How far is $47$ from the next ten?

steps.text: The next ten after $47$ is $50$. The ones need a bond to $10$: $7 + 3 = 10$.
Steps to a benchmark are always bonds: to reach $400$ from $364$ you need $36$.
